text:
zoe: quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC: if EU primary is unreachable, do we ever execute writes in non-EU land or should we always proxy-only/queue until primary returns? need a short policy and owners.

dan: we sketched three modes: block, proxy-only (accept request but don't persist outside region), and execute+escrow. we didn't pick a default.

kevin: runtime reality: proxy-only is possible if the standby can forward IO to a remote EU KV synchronously (adds latency) or if we implement a write-proxy that returns 202 while forwarding to EU. execute+escrow is already partially in the runtime as "staged-apply".

legal-bot: rule: for data flagged as "residency:EU" processing or storage outside EU is prohibited without explicit documented consent. Consent must be tenant-scoped, time-stamped, and revocable.

ops: operator concerns: execute+escrow increases complexity for reconciliation and increases operator surface area. need queue-aging metrics and an auto-cork if backlog grows.

devx: API suggestion: new header X-Residence-Mode: block|proxy-forward|execute-escrow. default=block. Also return a machine-readable reason when blocked.

ria: UX: customers should be able to pre-authorize cross-region on tenant settings page. show the current residency status and consent history.

zoe: proposal for a simple concrete default + opt-ins:
- default: block (fail-fast) for all tenants.
- opt-in: enterprise tenants can enable execute-escrow with consent token; non-sensitive tenants can enable proxy-forward.

kevin: for execute-escrow we must require an idempotency_key. reconciliation flow: standby executes, stores escrow record {idempotency_key, tenant, origin_region, payload_hash, result_ref}. when EU primary returns it replays deduping on idempotency_key.

sam.k: question: who bills for the standby execution? do we charge at time-of-execute or only on final apply?

kevin: bill at time-of-execute on standby. reconciliation is metadata-only and not charged for tokens again. add billing flag executor_billed=true.

legal-bot: consent token schema: CONSENT::{tenant_id}::{consent_id}::{timestamp}::{scopes}. Keep consent audit for 7 years.

ops: runbook items: add metrics: residency_block_rate, proxy_forward_latency_ms, escrow_queue_age_ms, escrow_depth. add circuit-breaker: if escrow_depth>5000 or queue_age>300s then disable execute-escrow globally.

devx: sample error response suggested:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error":"RESIDENCY_FORBIDDEN",
  "code":"RESIDENCY_BLOCKED",
  "explanation":"Tenant policy: EU-only. No consent recorded.",
  "help":"Set X-Residence-Mode or contact support"
}
```

ria: who owns what? propose owners:
- kevin: runtime changes (escrow + proxy-forward)
- devx: header + error payloads + docs
- ops: runbook + metrics
- legal-bot: consent schema + retention
- zoe: RFC follow-up PR and tenant opt-in UX

sam.k: timeline? RFC patch by Fri EOD, runtime spike next week, docs + API PR before runtime rollout.

dan: small note on cache: any response produced by execute-escrow must be labeled X-Redwood-Finality: pending|final. clients can request only-final reads. cache layers must not replicate embeddings for pending writes.

kevin: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
POST /v1/gen
Headers: X-Residence-Mode: execute-escrow
Body: { tenant_id:"t-999", residency:"EU" }
Server:
1) validate consent -> if missing and mode!=block return 403
2) if primary reachable -> normal apply
3) if primary down and mode=proxy-forward -> proxy to remote EU endpoint (sync)
4) if primary down and mode=execute-escrow -> execute on standby, store escrow record, return 202 + escrow_token
```

zoe: ok. I'll land the RFC patch with those defaults and owners. closing when PR merged. thanks all :rocket:
